question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` become a fixed 1 MiB maximum, despite previously accepting larger valid JSON files, and if so what user-visible compatibility contract should support that change?
rationale: The patch improves memory bounding but changes an existing CLI input path from unbounded acceptance to rejection; code review cannot choose the acceptable maximum or upgrade policy without Browser ownership intent.

options.title: Define and support a public limit
options.body: Accept a fixed limit only after documenting the rationale and user-facing behavior, then add boundary and upgrade-oriented proof for the chosen contract.

options.title: Preserve existing acceptance
options.body: Do not add a rejecting size limit until a compatible bounded-processing design is available for larger valid field descriptors.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or defer the PR if the Browser area does not want to establish a permanent fields-file size policy.

recommendation.title: Define and support a public limit
recommendation.body: Accept a fixed limit only after documenting the rationale and user-facing behavior, then add boundary and upgrade-oriented proof for the chosen contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate based on adjacent current-main Browser-plugin decisions; direct ownership history was not available to inspect.
